Measure per request and decode step: draft latency (ms), target verification latency (ms), acceptance rate by position (%), accepted tokens per step (tokens), synchronization/barrier and scheduler overhead (ms), queue wait (ms), time-to-first-token and end-to-end p50/p95/p99 latency (ms), decode throughput (tokens/s), draft/target GPU and CPU utilization (%), memory and KV-cache occupancy (MiB), transfers (MiB), errors/timeouts, and exact output-quality/equivalence checks. Trace timestamps and causal attribution for draft, verification, batching, transfers, idle gaps, retries, evictions, and fallback. Stratify by prompt/output length (tokens), concurrency, arrival burst rate, cache state, model/workload class, and acceptance profile.

Controlled experiment: randomize identical requests across target-only, current speculative, and current-plus-speculative KV admission arms, using matched warmup, fixed seeds/configuration, identical admission limits, and predeclared sample size. Compare paired per-request deltas with confidence intervals; use a held-out replay and an unchanged-load canary. Report both aggregate and workload-stratified results, and test interaction with concurrency and cache state. Control confounders from batching, autoscaling, thermal throttling, cache warmup, prompt mix, telemetry overhead, and background load; do not infer causality from aggregate averages alone.

Boundaries and rollback: begin with a small target-only/current/intervention canary. Fail closed to current speculative or target-only decoding on stale telemetry, dependency/version mismatch, quality or exactness failure, memory pressure, error-rate increase, queue/SLO breach, or quota violation. Disable the intervention and preserve traces/configuration for diagnosis if any guardrail trips; impose hard caps on extra draft work, memory, queue wait, and cost. Do not claim benefit without repeated randomized trials and domain review.
